comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official SBE Outline Study Programme for Bachelor Business Analytics 2026-2027 (s2), which states that it is a nominal plan based on the Bachelor Education and Examination Regulations (Chapter XVI) and quotes the credit structure: years 1 and 2 each comprise eight compulsory 6.5-EC courses and two compulsory 4-EC skills trainings (60 EC per year); the final phase comprises a 26-EC study-abroad period, an 8-EC Bachelor's Thesis, two 6.5-EC electives and one 13-EC Research Project or regional Internship (60 EC). The 2025-2026 outline (s3) and the public programme and courses-and-curriculum pages (s0, s1) show the same course list. Every course's EC weight and content (used for alignment) was verified in the official UM Course Descriptions Application (s4, 2026-2027 calendar, searched by course code). The Education and Examination Regulations were not separately consulted because the outline reproduces their credit text and no conflict between official sources was found. The programme has no formal routes, tracks or specializations. Two choices were instantiated: the 13-EC slot is recorded as the Research Project (EBP2001) rather than the alternative regional Internship Project (EBP2003), and the 26-EC study-abroad semester is recorded as such although the official outline states that students who do not study abroad complete elective courses instead; the two 6.5-EC electives are genuine open elective space and are preserved as such rather than filled with invented content.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Data science and data-driven analysis of business problems: data cleaning, exploration, visualisation and data-mining and prediction methods
Mathematics and statistics for analytics: calculus, linear algebra, probability, sampling, statistical inference and regression
Programming, databases and the computational implementation of models: Python, R, SQL, algorithms and optimisation modelling
Machine learning and AI methods and their business and organisational applications
Responsible data use: data ethics, privacy and the responsible use of AI
Business functions as recurring application domains: accounting, finance and risk, marketing and operations
Decision theory and business decision-making: choice, microeconomic and behavioural models translated into organisational decisions
Real organisational data cases and the communication of analytical results through eLab projects, reports and presentations
Independent applied research: a supervised research project and a bachelor thesis
questions: Using data and AI to create smart, responsible solutions for business and society

alternatives.label: Data Analytics, Machine Learning and Business Decisions
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum is dominated by UCR's data science, AI, mathematics and computer-science cluster (14 of 24 courses: Introduction to Programming, Mathematical Methods, Introduction to Data Science, Linear Algebra, Probability & Statistics, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, Database Management Systems, AI Ethics, Decision-making in AI, Optimization Methods in AI, Computational & Numerical Methods, Algorithms & Data Structures, and Research Methods & Statistics), complemented by a substantial business, economics and finance cluster (Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations, Introduction to Economics, Business & Economy in the Age of AI, Accounting & Corporate Finance, Money Banking & Finance, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Market Research, Econometrics) and one team research project. A single-field label such as Data Science would hide the business half of the programme, and a Business label would hide its technical majority, so the label names both strands and the decision focus.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response to the Bachelor Business Analytics at Maastricht University: a programme that combines the target's own core strands, using data and AI to solve business problems. It pairs UCR's data science, machine learning, programming, database, mathematics and statistics courses with UCR's accounting, finance, marketing, market-research and microeconomic decision-theory courses, adds AI ethics and AI-in-business courses for the target's responsible-data emphasis, uses optimisation, planning and algorithm courses for its modelling and operations content, and closes with a team research project on an externally posed problem. UCR offers no dedicated eLab-style analytics case courses, operations or supply-chain management, or R and web-development skills trainings, and those limitations are preserved in the comparison.
progression: DISGATE101 (semester 1) and DISGATE102 and BENGATE102 (semester 2), none of which has a prerequisite, precede every course that formally requires them: DISARIN211 and DISCOMP311 (semester 5) and DISARIN311 (semester 6) require DISGATE101; DISMATH314 and DISMATH211 (semester 3) and DISMATH213 and DISDATA311 (semester 4) require DISGATE102; BENENTR211 (semester 4) and BENECON312 (semester 6) require BENGATE102; and BENBUSI312 and BENENTR311 (semester 6) require BENGATE101 (semester 1). Advisory progression is followed where feasible: Introduction to Programming and Introduction to Data Science are in semester 1; probability and statistics, linear algebra and Machine Learning (semester 3) follow Mathematical Methods (semester 2) and precede Neural Networks & Deep Learning (semester 4), Econometrics (semester 6) and Optimization Methods in AI (semester 6, after Decision-making in AI in semester 5); Accounting & Corporate Finance (semester 5) precedes Money, Banking & Finance (semester 6); and Marketing & Consumer Engagement (semester 4) precedes Market Research (semester 6). Personal & Professional Development is in semester 1.

Mathematical Modelling, Optimisation and Algorithmic AI Engineering

selection.assessment: Alternative 1 directly owns eleven generator-eligible rows (5628, 5629, 5631, 5632, 5633, 5634, 5640, 5642, 5649, 5650, 5651) that describe the programme's own integrated identity: data science, statistics, programming, machine learning, AI in organisations, business decision-making, real organisational cases, reporting and independent analytics research. Three further candidate directions were assessed and rejected. (1) Analytics for business functions and economic decision-making (generating row 5648; supported by 5636-5639 and 5647) is evidenced by the target's Marketing, Financial Analysis, Accounting and Decision Theory courses (the last is in fact microeconomics, game theory and behavioural economics). A draft twenty-four-course version was tested against Alternative 1: Alternative 1 already carries the target's own accounting, finance, marketing, market-research and microeconomic courses in proportion to their weight in the target, and only three further UCR courses are actually evidenced by the target (Microeconomics & Behavior, Behavioral Economics and Strategy & Digital Transformation, about 22.5 EC). That is below the four-course, 30-EC floor; reaching it would require adding macroeconomics, persuasion or leadership courses that the target's evidence does not support, so the candidate is not-substantively-distinct rather than a genuine second route. (2) Mathematical modelling, optimisation and algorithmic AI engineering (generating rows 5630 and 5646) is already covered by the fourteen technical courses of Alternative 1 (mathematics, statistics, programming, machine learning, optimisation and algorithms); a more mathematical or computer-science curriculum would differ mainly through courses such as Reinforcement Learning, Linear Systems and Robotics that lie outside the target's evidence and would drop evidenced business components, so it is also not-substantively-distinct. (3) Responsible data and AI governance (generating row 5641) rests on the single compulsory Responsible Data Use course and the programme's stated ethical concern, which Alternative 1 already implements through AI Ethics and Business & Economy in the Age of AI; it cannot support a coherent 24-course programme and is rejected for insufficient evidence. No adjacent directions or question-led themes with target-specific evidence remain, so production stops at one alternative.

blocks: Introduction, business context and academic foundations

Business & Economy in the Age of AI directly addresses an important and identifiable part of Introduction to Business Analytics' subject, how business and data or AI connect, including AI's capabilities and limits, privacy and ethics through business cases; it does not teach the introductory data-analytic techniques (clustering, prediction, visualisation) or the group case project of that component.

Mathematical Methods directly addresses the calculus and mathematical-modelling half of Mathematics and Statistics 1 (differentiation, integration and applied modelling projects); its statistics half (descriptive statistics, probability and sampling) is covered by other UCR courses on separate rows.

Linear Algebra directly addresses the linear-algebra half of Mathematics and Statistics 2 (matrices, systems of linear equations, vector spaces and transformations); the statistical-inference half is covered by other UCR courses on separate rows.
Introduction to Programming directly implements the target's Fundamentals of Programming: Python, data types, control structures, and the steps from problem to implemented programme.

Database Management Systems directly implements relational database design, SQL querying and query processing, the core of the target's Database Management; its managerial and non-relational topics are not specifically covered.

Optimization Methods in AI addresses an important and identifiable part of Modelling and Computing's subject, computational optimisation of constrained problems through search and constraint satisfaction; it does not teach the integer linear programming, maximum-flow or dynamic-programming techniques of that component, and the difference in scope is material.
Data science, machine learning, AI and responsible data use

Introduction to Data Science directly addresses the data cleaning, exploration and visualisation of Knowledge Discovery and Data Visualization; the data-mining methods and model-evaluation techniques of that component are covered mainly by Machine Learning.

Machine Learning directly implements the supervised and unsupervised learning, classification and tree-based methods of the target's Machine Learning; the target's neural-network topics continue in the separate Neural Networks & Deep Learning course.
AI Ethics directly addresses the ethics, privacy, fairness and accountability parts of Responsible Data Use; the target's legal and data-protection element is not covered by any scheduled UCR course.

Introduction to Economics directly addresses Data-Driven Decision Theory's consumer and producer theory, market structures and game theory; the target's revealed-preference and behavioural-economics topics are not specifically covered.

Marketing & Consumer Engagement directly addresses the marketing concepts, strategy and functions of Marketing and Business Analytics; the target's data-driven segmentation, response-model and conjoint methods are not specifically covered.

Money, Banking & Finance directly addresses the financial decision-making and risk-assessment part of Financial Analysis and Risk Management; UCR does not evidence the valuation theory, portfolio theory and derivatives of that component.
Accounting & Corporate Finance directly addresses the financial-statement and accounting-theory part of Accounting and Technology; the data-analytics-in-accounting element is not covered.

Study abroad and open elective space

notes.text: Both programmes include substantial study of data science, mathematics, statistics, programming, machine learning, finance, marketing and decision-making. The Bachelor Business Analytics additionally includes two eLab data-challenge courses (with GIS-based decision-support systems), operations and supply-chain management, skills trainings in R, Python and web development, and two reporting skills courses, and a supervised research project and thesis. UCR students can instead combine Introduction to Data Science, Machine Learning, Neural Networks & Deep Learning, optimisation and algorithm courses, a team research project on an externally posed problem and UCR's standardised Optional independent research, but those specialist components are not offered at the same level of depth.

The Bachelor Business Analytics organises its third year around a study-abroad semester (students who do not go abroad take elective courses instead), two open electives, a research project and the thesis, so about 60 EC of the target's curriculum is open or externally located space that no UCR course can defensibly represent. The UCR programme instead distributes comparable territory across its own courses in data science, mathematics, computer science, economics and business, so it covers related ground through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the target course by course.
